messages:
maria: Heads-up — saw recurring short spikes in queue depth for the us-west2 gpu pool around 02:00 UTC this week. Dashboards show sharp p99 increases but median looks fine. Thinking sampling/resolution on the headroom panels might be hiding the early signal.
cheng: Hmm, I noticed that too. The panel is using a 1m rate on `irate()` plus a 5m recording rule. Spikes shorter than 30s get smoothed out.
oliver: Can you paste the query?
maria: Panel query (simplified):
```
irate(redwood_queue_depth_total{pool="us-west2-gpu"}[1m])
```
Recording rule: `record: job:queue_depth:rate5m` -> `avg_over_time(irate(...)[5m])`
cheng: Right — two suggestions: reduce scrape and query windows for that panel (eg `irate(...[15s])` with 15s scrape for the exporter) OR add a high-res 'burst' recording rule that keeps 15s granularity for 30m after a saturation event.
maria: Adding high-res rules increases TSDB volume though — cost tradeoff.
tara: Could we do adaptive sampling instead? i.e., default = 1m, but when a pool's queue depth crosses a low threshold, enable a short-term high-res recording for that pool. We already emit an alert when queue_depth_rate > 0.05 for 10s. Hook that alert to create a short-lived recording job via the control plane?
oliver: I like the idea. Implementation routes: 1) Prometheus rule + webhook to our control plane that toggles a scrape job with label matchers; 2) Use Cortex/Thanos downsampled plus raw short-retention shard for high-res slices; 3) Use exemplars (trace ids) to mark interesting series and then pull raw metrics from a collector for a short window.
cheng: Option 2 requires more infra (short-retention bucket) but is safer. Option 1 is simpler: controller listens to alertmanager webhook and creates Job CRD that sets scrape_interval for that pool's exporter to 15s for 20m. We need to ensure exporter supports per-pool override.
infra-bot: Note: last config change touching exporters was `prometheus-exporter-config:v6` on 1823430000 — no recent changes.
maria: For Grafana panel UX, we should add a toggle variable `$resolution` that switches queries between `15s`, `30s`, `60s`. Also add an annotation when adaptive sampling is active (from control plane) so SREs see why spikes look different.
tara: Alert tuning: current queue-depth alert fires on sustained 1m average which misses short burst saturation. We should add a short-burst alert (30s window) to trigger the adaptive sampling and an aggregator alert that fires only if bursts persist for >5m. Keeps noisy one-shot alerts from paging.
olch: (typo)
oliver: Agree on two-tier alerts. Also add a metric for `batch_saturation_ratio{pool}` that tries to capture when batch size/latency interplay causes reduced throughput — can help correlate with queue spikes.
cheng: For cost cap: if we enable high-res for many pools simultaneously, TSDB/RAM could spike. Add a global budget of N concurrent high-res pools and a priority queue (prod > staging). The controller should enforce it and fallback to sampling 30s if budget is exhausted.
maria: I'll sketch a prototype for the controller + recording-rule approach and demo on staging us-west2. Steps: 1) recording rule for high-res series (namespace pool label) 2) Alertmanager webhook -> controller 3) controller toggles a ConfigMap with override that a promoter picks up 4) Grafana panel switch + annotation stream
tara: Add runbook section too: how to manually force high-res for a pool, how to escalate if controller fails.
oliver: Can someone open a RFC? I'll help with queries and resource estimates. Include back-of-envelope TSDB cost for 15s -> 1m retention slices.
maria: Creating RFC ticket: RFC-18234 (will link). Demo plan targeted for next week's dry-run.
cheng: I'll run a quick script to simulate short bursts (k6 for the request queue) and measure data ingestion impact.
maria: Thanks — tagging @oncall for visibility once we have alert changes. :eyes: :rocket:
infra-bot: action: recording_rule_proposal.md attached to ticket RFC-18234 (internal link).
